why: The outer shape gets one more side each time: 3, 4, 5, so next is a 6-sided hexagon. The small oval inside takes turns: standing, lying, standing, so next it is lying. Option 2 is a hexagon with a lying oval. Option 1 has a standing oval and option 3 a big round one.
trick: Look at the outer shape and the inner shape separately; each has its own rule.
note: Options B and D differ only in the small tilt of the oval (B rises to the right, D falls to the right); the rule cannot separate them, so B is taken from the book key.
